annotations.description: Chose to be on the draw (letting opponent go first) without knowing the matchup. In competitive Magic, going first is almost always advantageous as it gives tempo advantage - you play lands and threats a turn earlier. The reasoning even states 'there's a slight statistical advantage to choosing to play first' but then contradicts itself by choosing to go second. The reasoning text appears to cut off mid-sentence, suggesting confused logic.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to let the opponent (MiMo Minimal) take the first turn, putting themselves on the draw.
annotations.betterLine: Choose to play first (select Sonnet Critic as starting player) for the standard tempo advantage of being on the play, which is correct in the vast majority of matchups, especially when the matchup is unknown.

annotations.description: With only 1 mana available (Blood Crypt), the player chose Seal of Fire over Nethergoyf. Nethergoyf as a 1/2 (creature type in graveyard from Street Wraith) provides a body that can block and apply pressure, while Seal of Fire is merely a 2-damage removal spell sitting on the battlefield. However, Seal of Fire does add an enchantment type to the graveyard when sacrificed, which would grow Nethergoyf later. The key consideration is that Nethergoyf could have been cast now as a 1/2 and would grow as more card types enter the graveyard, while Seal of Fire doesn't impact the board meaningfully on its own. That said, Seal of Fire provides flexible removal and adds a card type to graveyard (enchantment) when used, so this is debatable rather than clearly wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Seal of Fire with the one available black/red mana from Blood Crypt.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Nethergoyf as a 1/2 creature that can grow over time, providing an early board presence and blocker. Seal of Fire could be cast next turn alongside a land drop for Island, enabling future Expressive Iteration or Counterspell mana.

annotations.description: With Expressive Iteration, the standard play is to put the non-land card into hand and exile the land to play it this turn. By putting Undercity Sewers into hand, they'll lose access to Moonshadow (either exiling or bottoming it). Taking Moonshadow to hand and exiling Swamp would have netted both a creature and a land drop.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Undercity Sewers (tapped land) into hand, losing access to Moonshadow
annotations.betterLine: Put Moonshadow into hand, exile Swamp to play it this turn as an untapped land drop, bottom Undercity Sewers

annotations.description: Discarding Goryo's Vengeance when there's no legendary creature in the graveyard to target, but the card has future potential. The player has Solitude in hand which could be evoked (putting it in the graveyard) and then targeted with Goryo's Vengeance for a powerful tempo play with Ephemerate to make it permanent. Discarding one copy is acceptable since they have two, but Winternight Stories or one of the Ephemerates might be better discard candidates. Winternight Stories is a 3-mana sorcery that draws 3 and discards (decent but slow), while the Goryo's + Ephemerate + Solitude combo is the deck's primary game plan. Having two Goryo's Vengeance provides redundancy for this critical combo piece.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Goryo's Vengeance to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard Winternight Stories instead, preserving both copies of Goryo's Vengeance for maximum combo redundancy. Winternight Stories is a slower card advantage spell that's less critical than combo pieces, especially when the deck wants to execute Solitude + Goryo's Vengeance + Ephemerate.

annotations.description: Casting Thoughtseize before playing Undercity Sewers is slightly suboptimal sequencing. Undercity Sewers enters tapped so it won't help cast anything this turn, but playing it first would trigger surveil 1, putting a card into the graveyard which could add a third card type (land) to the graveyard for Nethergoyf (currently 2 types: sorcery and creature). More importantly, the land drop costs no mana and should generally be done before spending mana on spells. Additionally, Thoughtseize costs 2 life (going to 16), and the life loss matters for Death's Shadow. The sequencing error is minor since the Undercity Sewers enters tapped anyway and doesn't change available mana this turn, but the surveil information could have informed the Thoughtseize decision.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thoughtseize before playing Undercity Sewers
annotations.betterLine: Play Undercity Sewers first (surveil 1 to potentially grow Nethergoyf and gain information), then cast Thoughtseize with Blood Crypt

annotations.description: Taking Goryo's Vengeance over Solitude is debatable. Solitude is the opponent's best removal spell and can be evoked for free to exile key threats like Death's Shadow or Moonshadow. Goryo's Vengeance currently has no legendary creatures in the opponent's graveyard to reanimate (only Polluted Delta and the Goryo's Vengeance itself are there), making it a lower immediate threat. Solitude, on the other hand, is always live as premium removal that can blow out the Sonnet Critic's game plan. However, Goryo's Vengeance could become very dangerous if a Quantum Riddler or Solitude ends up in the graveyard later, and denying a reanimation combo piece has merit. The opponent also has Ephemerate x2 which combos powerfully with Solitude (evoke Solitude, then Ephemerate it to keep it and get another exile trigger), but taking Solitude would break up that combo more directly.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Goryo's Vengeance from opponent's hand
annotations.betterLine: Discard Solitude to remove the opponent's best removal spell and break up the Solitude + Ephemerate combo, which would generate massive value if assembled

annotations.description: Fetched basic Swamp when hand contains mostly blue and white spells (Quantum Riddler, Winternight Stories, 2x Ephemerate, Solitude). Basic Swamp only provides black for Thoughtseize, while a dual land like Watery Grave would provide both black AND blue mana for the heavily blue hand, at the cost of just 2 life from a healthy 17 life total.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched basic Swamp from Polluted Delta
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Watery Grave (paying 2 life to enter untapped) to have access to both U and B mana, supporting both Thoughtseize this turn and future blue spells like Quantum Riddler and Winternight Stories.

annotations.description: By casting the second Nethergoyf, Sonnet Critic taps out completely and loses the ability to hold up Counterspell (UU) with their remaining untapped lands (Island + Undercity Sewers). The opponent has two Goryo's Vengeance in their graveyard and could have threatening plays. With only a Swamp on board, the opponent's options are limited this turn, but leaving up Counterspell provides insurance against future threats. The second Nethergoyf is also only a 2/3 - modest additional pressure. However, Moonshadow for {B} would have been a similar option that provides a 1/1 with menace that can grow, though also prevents holding up Counterspell. The key tension is between deploying threats and holding countermagic.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast a second Nethergoyf (2/3) for {B}, tapping out completely with no counterspell protection available.
annotations.betterLine: Hold up Counterspell by not casting another creature this turn. The opponent could draw into dangerous plays like a reanimation target + enabler, and having Counterspell ready is more valuable than an extra 2/3 body when you already have a Nethergoyf and Seal of Fire on board.

annotations.description: MiMo Minimal missed the classic Solitude + Ephemerate combo line. They could evoke Solitude (exiling one Ephemerate as the white card), exile one Nethergoyf with the ETB, then cast the second Ephemerate to blink Solitude (dodging the evoke sacrifice trigger), exile the second Nethergoyf with the re-entry ETB, and end up with a 3/2 lifelink on board with Ephemerate on rebound. The opponent's lands were all tapped, so there was no interaction available. Instead, they cast Thoughtseize into an opponent who already had their threats deployed on board.

annotations.betterLine: Evoke Solitude (exiling one Ephemerate), targeting a Nethergoyf with ETB, then cast second Ephemerate on Solitude to blink it and exile the second Nethergoyf, ending with a 3/2 lifelink and Ephemerate rebound

annotations.description: MiMo Minimal attempted to cast Quantum Riddler for {3}{U}{U} but only has 2 lands (Meticulous Archive and Swamp), making it impossible to pay the mana cost. The game engine rolled back the action. Meanwhile, Solitude could have been cast via its Evoke cost (exile a white card from hand) — MiMo has Ephemerate as a white card to exile. Solitude's ETB would exile one of the opponent's creatures (like a Nethergoyf), and then Ephemerate could be cast in response to the Evoke sacrifice trigger to blink Solitude, keeping it on the battlefield and getting a second exile trigger. This is a classic Solitude + Ephemerate combo that would remove two of the opponent's threats while keeping a 3/2 lifelink creature.

annotations.betterLine: Evoke Solitude (exiling Ephemerate as the white card), targeting a Nethergoyf with the ETB exile trigger, then cast the second Ephemerate on Solitude in response to the Evoke sacrifice trigger to keep Solitude and exile a second creature. This would devastate the opponent's board.

annotations.description: Sonnet Critic had Bloodstained Mire available to activate during combat. Sacrificing it would put a land card into the graveyard, adding 'Land' as a card type among cards in the graveyard (currently Creature, Sorcery from Death's Shadow, Expressive Iteration, Street Wraith, Thoughtseize). This would increase Nethergoyf's power from 2 to 3 each, making the attack deal 3+3+1=7 damage instead of 2+2+1=5. Opponent goes from 8 to 1 life instead of 3, and then Seal of Fire deals exactly 2 damage for lethal (or even just 1 would suffice). With the fetch crack, the total would be 7 combat + 2 Seal of Fire = 9 damage against 8 life, which is lethal even accounting for the 1 life paid to crack the fetch.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without activating Bloodstained Mire, dealing only 5 combat damage (2+2+1) leaving opponent at 3 life.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Bloodstained Mire before combat damage resolves to add Land as a card type to the graveyard, pumping both Nethergoyfs to 3/4. This makes combat damage 3+3+1=7, putting opponent to 1 life. Then sacrifice Seal of Fire for 2 damage for lethal. Net life cost is 1 life from the fetch, but the opponent is dead.

annotations.description: Chose to exile the second Nethergoyf (2/3) instead of Moonshadow (currently 1/1 but can grow to 7/7 as permanents enter graveyard). Moonshadow has menace and will grow - the evoke sacrifice of Solitude itself will remove a counter, and future fetchland/permanent sacrifices will continue to grow it.
